{{Quote|Knowing that you, the people of Agamar, are here, supporting us, will brighten the darkest hour and lighten the heaviest load.|Leia Organa Solo addresses the Agamarian Council|<ref name="DTI:O" />}}
'''Agamar''' was an [[Agriworld/Legends|agriworld]] in the [[Mirgoshir system/Legends|Mirgoshir system]] of the [[Lahara sector/Legends|Lahara sector]]. At one [[Time/Legends|time]] part of the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakatan]] [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]] and home to an [[underwater civilization]], Agamar became part of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] prior to the [[New Sith Wars]] and later joined the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] shortly before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. The site of fighting between Republic and Separatist forces, it was once more in Republic hands by the end of the Clone Wars, and subsequently became part of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Resistance to Imperial rule led to the [[Destruction of Tondatha|destruction]] of the small town of [[Tondatha]] as punishment, after which the [[Agamar Resistance]] joined the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. Agamar, however, remained in Imperial hands for several more years, before eventually joining the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. During the early stages of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], Agamar took in refugees from worlds hit by the [[Yuuzhan Vong]], but eventually fell to the invaders. By the [[Second Galactic Civil War]], the [[Planet/Legends|world]] was once more under [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial]] control, and remained part of the [[Fel Empire]] in the following decades. During the [[Second Imperial Civil War]], Agamar was part of deposed [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Roan Fel]]'s [[Empire-in-exile]] and served as the site of a meeting between Fel and the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]].

Agamar had a mostly [[Human/Legends|Human]] population and was governed by the [[Agamarian Council]] in its [[Capital/Legends|capital]] city of [[Calna Muun]]. As something of a backwater planet, Agamar was not a well-known world. Among those who had heard of the planet, [[Agamarian]]s were stereotyped as dumb hicks, though many natives of the world played important roles in both the Rebel Alliance and New Republic, most notably the New Republic [[General/Legends|general]] and [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Keyan Farlander/Legends|Keyan Farlander]].

==Description==
{{Quote|Ahh. Agamar. I was there once. Nice planet.|[[Halley Kadorto]]|<ref name="XW:TOSG" />}}
Agamar was a small [[Planet/Legends|world]],<ref name="XW:TOSG" /> located in the [[Mirgoshir system/Legends|Mirgoshir system]]<ref name="EGPM" /> in the [[New Territories/Legends|New Territories]].<ref name="Region" /> It was situated near the [[Mirgoshir system/Legends|Mirgoshir hyperspace crossroads]]—<ref name="NEC" /> the intersection of the [[Braxant Run/Legends|Braxant Run]] and [[Celanon Spur/Legends|Celanon Spur]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]]<ref name="TEA" />—which eventually became a key route between the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] and [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]].<ref name="DTII:R">''[[The New Jedi Order: Dark Tide II: Ruin]]''</ref> Although one of 245 settled worlds in the [[Lahara sector/Legends|Lahara sector]],<ref name="EGPM" /><ref name="HNN">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|50|news/1344_4.html|Lahara Sector Secedes}}</ref> its location within the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] left it largely secluded from the rest of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]<ref name="EGPM" /> and, as a result, it was often regarded as a backwater world by many within the [[galactic community]].<ref name="XW:TOSG" />

[[File:Binka.png|thumb|left|250px|A binka forest]]
A terrestrial world, Agamar's surface featured several landmasses separated by [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]],<ref name="EGPM" /> including the [[Bil Da'Gari]]<ref name="RC:TC" /> and the [[Crescent Sea]].<ref name="TOR SotD" /> The climate was warm and dry,<ref name="DTI:O" /> though the planet had large expanses of arable land.<ref name="NJOS" /> Over [[Time/Legends|time]], natural bridges had developed on the planet's surface.<ref name="DB">{{DB|vehicle|utat|Unstable Terrain Artillery Transport (UT-AT)}}</ref> Much of the land was covered with forests of [[binka]] [[Tree/Legends|trees]]<ref name="EGPM" />—these trees, native to Agamar, grew regularly spaced, and as such became popular amongst youngsters to maneuver [[Repulsorcraft/Legends|repulsorcraft]] through at high speeds.<ref name="XW:TOSG" /> The world developed a reputation as a rough planet where it was difficult to survive,<ref name="XW:WS">''[[X-Wing: Wraith Squadron]]''</ref> yet despite its reputation, those who visited Agamar would later comment on its natural beauty.<ref name="XW:TOSG" />

Among the planet's indigenous fauna was the [[mugruebe]], a small [[Mammal/Legends|mammal]] roughly twice the size of a [[Womp rat/Legends|womp rat]].<ref name="XW:TOSG" /> Often [[Farm/Legends|farmed]] at ranches,<ref name="EGPM" /> the creatures were the main ingredient in the local dish, [[mugruebe stew]], together with roots and bark from the planet's trees. Although mugruebe stew was popular among the [[Agamarian]] population, it remained largely unpopular throughout the galaxy.<ref name="XW:TOSG" /> During the years surrounding the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], however, at least one [[Agamar slider|Agamarian dish]] was served as far away as [[Dex's Diner/Legends|Dex's Diner]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. The [[Vegetarian/Legends|meatless]] [[slider]] included a patty made from [[Agamarian soybean]]s topped with a slice of [[binka fruit]] and [[mugruebe spit-sauce]].<ref name="DaD">{{Hyperspace|url=fans/hyperspace/source/dexdiner/index.html|text=Dining at Dex's|int=Dining at Dex's}}</ref> Other fauna included a [[Agamarian beast|species]] of quadrupeds with four eyes, thick tails and bone protrusions rising from a flared crest at the rear of the head. These creatures were used as beasts of burden by Agamarian farmers.<ref name="Legacy45" />

==History==
===Pre-Republic===
Around [[30,000 BBY]], during the [[Pre-Republic era]], the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakatans]] spread out from their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[Lehon/Legends|Lehon]] and established the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]], which would dominate much of the galaxy for almost five thousand years. Agamar was one of many worlds brought under Rakatan control during this time. With the collapse of the Empire in [[25,200 BBY]], the Rakata retreated to their homeworld, leaving little trace as to how and why they left.<ref name="TEA" /> At some point during Agamar's early history, an [[underwater civilization]] existed on the floor of the Crescent Sea. This civilization was long-extinct by the time of the [[Great Galactic War]].<ref name="TOR SotD" />

===Galactic Republic===
Though located in an area of the galaxy which was not fully explored until between [[3000 BBY|3000]] and [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]],<ref name="TEA" /> Agamar itself was known to the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] as early as the Great Galactic War.<ref name="TOR Sith">{{Holonet|allegiances|sith-empire|The Sith Empire}}</ref> Beginning with the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire's]] surprise attack on the Republic in [[3681 BBY]],<ref name="TOR timeline">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 6: Onslaught of the Sith Empire|int=Timeline 6: Onslaught of the Sith Empire}}</ref> the Great Galactic War saw the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] quickly seize control of several Outer Rim [[Star system/Legends|systems]], winning numerous victories over Republic forces, including [[Battle of Agamar (Great Galactic War)|one battle]] fought in the forests of Agamar.<ref name="TOR Sith" /> A decade after the end of the Great Galactic War, Agamar was represented in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] by the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Oranda]].<ref name="Repairing Coruscant">{{TORcite|type=general|Repairing Coruscant|Coruscant}}</ref> Around this time, Agamar suffered from severe droughts which revealed the ruins of its former underwater civilization on the Crescent Sea floor. The discoverer attracted many scavengers to Agamar in the hopes of looting its treasures.<ref name="TOR SotD" /> During the [[Galactic War]] between the Republic and the Empire, a community of Agamarian farmers were driven insane by underground signals that seemed to be Rakatan in origin.<ref name="Shadow">{{TORcite|exp=shadow|type=crewskill|Scavenging|Emergent Echoes}}</ref> Following the end of the war, Agamar remained under Republic control during the [[New Sith Wars]] between [[2000 BBY/Legends|2000]] and 1000 BBY.<ref name="TEA" />

At some point during the Old Republic era, the planet suffered an infestation of [[Lyran bloodslug]]s. The [[Parasite/Legends|parasites]] left their homeworld of [[Lyran IV]] when a local [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] used one of them to infect a visiting [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]]. The spacer took his cargo of grain to trade on Agamar, where the parasite was able to multiply in the grain-rich [[Spaceport/Legends|starport]]. The creatures soon infested the starport, causing the [[Death/Legends|deaths]] of over 100 victims, the largest bloodslug infestation on record.<ref name="Creature Feature">{{Wizards|url=starwars/article.asp?x=sw20011213c_slug&c=rpg|series=Creature Feature|text=Lyran Bloodslug}}</ref> [[New Agamar]], also settled prior to the Clone Wars, was likely named after Agamar.<ref name="Jedi Trial">''[[Jedi Trial]]''</ref>

By [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]],<ref name="ERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> the planet, and the Mirgoshir system, was administered by [[Governor/Legends|Governor]] [[Challep]] and already had a reputation as a backwater world. The planet's [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] defenses were poor, with their starfighters unable to compete with the more advanced [[Z-95 Headhunter/Legends|Z-95 Headhunters]]. They were also forced to rely on [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]] to [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] the [[Starship/Legends|ships]], and most mercenaries at the time spent a few [[Standard month/Legends|months]] in Agamar's service.<ref name="ST">{{GamerCite|1|The Starfighter Trap}}</ref>

[[File:Agamar.jpg|thumb|ight|250px|Agamar]]
Challep, however, was committed to building an advanced planetary defense force, and set about replacing the system's starfighter contingent. The world purchased new starfighters, including Z-95s and at least 100 [[Vulture-class starfighter/Legends|Vulture droid starfighters]], along with other weapons technologies, including at least two [[Hornet-class carrier|''Hornet''-class carriers]]. They also attempted to hire additional pilots for the new ships. One such pilot was [[Dren Melne]], a [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]] who served in [[Bravo Squadron/Legends|Bravo Squadron]] of the [[Naboo Royal Space Fighter Corps/Legends|Naboo Royal Space Fighter Corps]], who was paid over 100,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] for his services.<ref name="ST" />

The Naboo's [[N-1 starfighter/Legends|N-1 starfighters]] and [[N-X Police Cruiser/Legends|N-X Police Cruisers]] represented the sort of technology Challep sought, and the Agamarians made at least three attempts to purchase some of the starfighters, only to be rejected each time by [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala's]] [[Naboo Royal Advisory Council/Legends|Royal Advisory Council]]. Melne convinced Challep that even buying the parts direct from [[Nubia Star Drives, Incorporated/Legends|Nubia Star Drives, Incorporated]] would not allow them to replicate the technology, so Challep organized a raid on the [[Naboo system/Legends|Naboo system]]. [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Sorran]] would lead the mission as two [[Carrier/Legends|carriers]] [[Battle at TFP-9|attacked]] [[Station TFP-9]] to draw out the Naboo defenses. After verifying their capabilities, Melne would turn on his own people to help the Agamarians disable some of the fighters to be returned to Agamar for study by engineers, with a view to replicating the technology.<ref name="ST" />

However, the mission went awry when Naboo fighter pilot [[Essara Till/Legends|Essara Till]], together with [[Echo Flight]], [[Starfighter combat/Legends|destroyed]] one of the carriers and forced Sorran to withdraw. Before fleeing, Sorran had Melne killed to prevent the Agamarians from learning the truth. Governor Challep denied any Agamarian involvement in the incident and no significant links were found between Agamar and Melne. The money placed in his account could not be tracked to its source. Even so, the Naboo requested that the Galactic Senate investigate the matter.<ref name="ST" />

In about [[31 BBY/Legends|31 BBY]],<ref name="LFC date">The ''[[Living Force Campaign Guide]]'' states that the [[Living Force (roleplaying campaign)|''Living Force'']] campaign is set one [[Standard year/Legends|year]] after the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]], an event that is placed in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] by ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''. Therefore, ''[[Trade Wars: Find the Lady|Find the Lady]]'' can be dated to circa [[31 BBY/Legends|31 BBY]].</ref> [[Maegyn]], the head chef of the [[Golden Cochlea]] restaurant on the planet [[Cularin/Legends|Cularin]], placed an order with [[Mothven Star Trading]], to send some binka tree bark from Agamar to his restaurant.<ref name="Consignment">{{LivingForce|Trade Wars: Consignment}}</ref>

===Clone Wars===
{{Quote|Salvage the remaining arms and withdraw the army. Bring them to Agamar.|Count Dooku, to General Kalani after the Battle of Onderon|<ref name="TP">{{TCW|Tipping Points}}</ref>}}
By [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], the planet was represented in the Galactic Senate by [[Tyreca Bremack]], [[Senator/Legends|senator]] for the Lahara sector. Towards the end of the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]], on 22:4:4 BBY, high taxation led Senator Bremack to [[Articles of Secession/Legends|announce]] the sector's secession from the Republic.<ref name="HNN" /> Bremack subsequently brought the Lahara sector into the growing [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], taking Agamar with it.<ref name="NEC" />

Later in 22 BBY, war broke out between the Republic and the Separatists. Agamar was drawn into the Clone Wars in the month following the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]] as the two sides fought a campaign for control of the Mirgoshir system.<ref name="NEC" /> Early fighting in the system went against the Republic, despite the efforts of their [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] pilots, and the Republic forces eventually withdrew from the system. Around this time, Agamar was one of several worlds to be [[Mirgoshir campaign|struck]] in devastating attacks by the ancient [[Force Harvester]], recently [[Conquest of Raxus Prime|uncovered]] by [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] on [[Raxus Prime/Legends|Raxus Prime]]. The Force Harvester was intended to power the [[Dark Reaper]], which Dooku's forces were excavating on [[Thule/Legends|Thule]]. Later that month, Republic forces struck at Thule and, during the subsequent [[Battle of Thule|battle]], the [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] was destroyed by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]]. Once Separatist forces withdrew from the [[Thurra system/Legends|Thurra system]], the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] prepared to move back into the Mirgoshir system, in an attempt to secure Agamar.<ref name="SW:TCW">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (video game)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' video game]]</ref> Four months after this attempt began, Separatist [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|armies]] were still fighting in the Mirgoshir system and unable to reinforce their comrades commanded by [[Shogar Tok]] on [[Brentaal IV/Legends|Brentaal IV]].<ref name="Jedi: Shaak Ti">''[[Jedi: Shaak Ti]]''</ref>

At some point during the [[Mirgoshir campaign]], as Republic forces clashed with Separatists on Agamar, the heavy footfalls of Republic [[Walker/Legends|walkers]] caused the natural bridges they were crossing to collapse beneath them, resulting in many vehicles and soldiers being lost. This disaster prompted [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards]] to team up with [[Mekuun Corporation/Legends|Mekuun]] to design the [[Unstable Terrain Artillery Transport/Legends|Unstable Terrain Artillery Transport]], which the Republic used successfully on worlds including [[Mygeeto/Legends|Mygeeto]] and [[Cato Neimoidia/Legends|Cato Neimoidia]].<ref name="DB" />

In 21 BBY, [[Sergeant/Legends|Sergeant]] [[Kal Skirata]] of the Grand Army of the Republic, together with the [[Advanced Recon Commando/Legends|Advanced Recon Commando]] [[Ordo Skirata|Null-11]], traveled to Agamar to purchase the [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] [[DeepWater-class light freighter|''DeepWater''-class light freighter]] ''[[Aay'han]]'' from a [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] [[Merchant/Legends|merchant]] in [[Calna Muun]], for use in a mission to locate the [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoan]] scientist [[Ko Sai/Legends|Ko Sai]].<ref name="RC:TC" />

Around [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]],<ref name="Death Sentence 1">[[Darth Maul — Death Sentence 1|''Darth Maul — Death Sentence'' 1]]</ref> following the victory of [[King/Legends|King]] [[Ramsis Dendup/Legends|Ramsis Dendup]] and the [[Royal Onderon Militia/Legends|Royal Onderon Militia]] over Separatist forces under the command of the [[Super tactical droid/Legends|super tactical droid]] [[General/Legends|General]] [[Kalani/Legends|Kalani]] at the [[Battle of Onderon/Legends|Battle of Onderon]], Count Dooku ordered Kalani to withdraw his [[Army/Legends|army]] and fall back to Agamar.<ref name="TP" />

===Galactic Empire===
{{Quote|People of Tondatha, on the planet of Agamar, in the Lahara sector … You have been found guilty of sedition against the Empire, and of plotting against the great Emperor Palpatine. Your punishment will be imposed without delay.|An Imperial commander pronounces sentence on Tondatha|<ref name="XW:TOSG" />}}
Following the end of the Clone Wars and the [[Declaration of a New Order]], Agamar became part of the newly formed [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] [[Oversector Outer]].<ref name="TEA" /> The world came to be seen as unimportant by the new galactic government and officials from the Empire rarely visited the world, though on at least one occasion approximately five years into the reign of [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], a small Imperial flotilla passed through the Lahara sector, stopping in [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] of Agamar and dispatching landing craft to the planet.<ref name="XW:TOSG" />

However, the Empire struggled to maintain complete control over distant worlds in the Outer Rim and, over time, resistance groups began to develop on many disenchanted Rim worlds.<ref name="EGPM" /> Agamar was one such world, and the [[Agamar Resistance]] formed<ref name="XW:TOSG" /> by [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]].<ref name="1BBY">''[[X-Wing: The Official Strategy Guide]]'' begins after the [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing starfighter]] entered service with the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], which ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' places in [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]]. ''X-Wing: The Official Strategy Guide'' establishes that the [[Battle of Tatooine (Galactic Civil War)|capture of Leia Organa]] occurs at the end of [[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']]{{'s}} second tour of duty. Organa's capture takes place on 35:3:3 under the [[Great ReSynchronization]] dating system, placing it at the beginning of [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] according to [[Template:YearMathGRS|the following explanation]]. Events in ''X-Wing: The Official Strategy Guide'' before the end of the second tour of duty therefore take place in 1 BBY.</ref> Based mainly out of Calna Muun,<ref name="EGPM" /> the movement attracted many who were opposed to Imperial rule but saw little opportunity to have a genuine effect on galactic affairs—despite Agamar's previous military buildup, only a handful of functioning Z-95s remained<ref name="XW:TOSG" />—and stayed outside of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]].<ref name="FP">{{StoryCite|story=The Farlander Papers|book=Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)}}</ref>

[[File:Agamar2.jpg|thumb|left|250px|An ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer moves to attack Tondatha.]]
Even so, news of insurgents on the remote world eventually reached the Empire, and an [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] was dispatched to Agamar to end the insurrection. As an assault craft descended into the [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] over the small town of [[Tondatha]], the Imperial commander announced that the inhabitants had been found guilty of sedition. The penalty for their supposed crime was severe—the Imperials poured [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolaser]] and [[Concussion missile/Legends|concussion missile]] fire down on the settlement, leaving the buildings as smoking ruins and many residents killed or seriously injured. So great was the level of [[Destruction of Tondatha|destruction]] that the survivors abandoned the ruins rather than rebuilding.<ref name="XW:TOSG" />

The Resistance was shaken by the massacre at Tondatha, but more determined than ever to find a way to strike back at the Empire.<ref name="EGPM" /> Several months after the destruction of Tondatha,<ref name="XW:TOSG" /> the [[Mon Calamari Star Cruiser/Legends|Mon Calamari Star Cruiser]] [[Independence/Legends|''Independence'']] arrived at Agamar, bringing [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]], former [[Chandrila/Legends|Chandrilan]] senator and current [[Chief of State (Alliance)/Legends|Chief of State]] of the Rebel Alliance, for a secret meeting to persuade the Resistance to join the Alliance. Around 200 members of the Resistance attended the meeting, held in an abandoned warehouse in Calna Muun, during which Mothma delivered a speech stressing the Empire's many atrocities and circulated the ''[[A Call to Reason]]'' pamphlet to persuade the attendees of the need to make a stand. Mon Mothma's visit had the desired result, and several of those present joined the crew of the ''Independence'' immediately, while Rebel advisors remained on Agamar to assist the Resistance.<ref name="FP" />

Following the [[Destruction of Alderaan/Legends|destruction]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] later that year, a refugee camp was established on Agamar for Alderaanians who had lost their home in the disaster. Through this refugee camp, the Rebel Alliance acquired several new members, including [[Kira Lar]], who made the journey to Agamar after hearing the news in the hopes of contacting the Rebellion.<ref name="Kira Lar, Human Rebel Soldier">{{Wizards|url=starwars/article.asp?x=npc_kira|text=Kira Lar, Human Rebel Soldier}}</ref>

===Fall of the Empire===
Rebel agitation did not, however, give the Alliance control of the planet, and Agamar long remained part of Imperial Space. During the [[Hunt for Zsinj|hunt]] for [[Warlord/Legends|Warlord]] [[Zsinj]] in [[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]], the Agamarian Captain [[Choday Hrakness]] was given command of the [[CR90 corvette/Legends|CR90 corvette]] [[Ession Strike|''Night Caller'']], after it was captured by [[Wraith Squadron]]. Shortly afterwards, the Wraiths took advantage of the Agamarian stereotype on a mission to infiltrate the Imperial world of [[Storinal]], when [[Garik Loran]], [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]], and [[Myn Donos]] disguised themselves as three yokel brothers from Agamar on a wife-hunting expedition.<ref name="XW:WS" />

In [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]], after the defeat of Zsinj, New Republic [[Supreme Commander (Alliance)/Legends|Supreme Commander]] [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Gial Ackbar]] led a campaign against the Imperial Remnant. Launching from [[Palanhi/Legends|Palanhi]] in the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]] Territories, Ackbar's forces captured [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]] before bringing Agamar under New Republic control. By [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]], Agamar had become a New Republic stronghold. However, after [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Mitth'raw'nuruodo]] returned from the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]] to lead the Imperial Remnant, Agamar was one of many worlds recaptured by the Empire as Thrawn's forces [[Thrawn campaign|advanced]] on the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]].<ref name="TEA" />

Agamar continued to change hands during the following years, falling out of Imperial control by [[10 ABY/Legends|10 ABY]], only to be brought back into the Imperial Remnant after Admiral [[Gilad Pellaeon/Legends|Gilad Pellaeon]] became [[Supreme Commander (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Supreme Commander]] in [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]].<ref name="TEA" /> That year, Agamar served as a rendezvous point where Admiral Pellaeon mustered his fleet in preparation for an [[Raid on Orinda|attack on Orinda]]. While the Imperials took on supplies and awaited Pellaeon's arrival, they deployed [[Immobilizer 418 Interdictor-class Heavy Cruiser|Immobilizer 418 cruisers]] to prevent passing traffic from [[Spy/Legends|spying]] on them. The Interdictors' [[Gravity well/Legends|gravity wells]] soon caused a New Republic ship transporting the captured renegade Jedi [[Dal Konur]] to [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]] to be pulled out of [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]], though they were able to escape. Around the same time, a medical quarantine of [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]] led to ships being diverted to Agamar, as well as [[Bandomeer/Legends|Bandomeer]].<ref name="Nightsaber">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20031120nightsaber|text=Nightsaber|int=Nightsaber}}</ref> When Pellaeon launched his attack on [[Orinda/Legends|Orinda]], he left the [[Star Dreadnought/Legends|Star Dreadnought]] ''[[Megador]]'' to defend Agamar from a possible New Republic attack from [[Celanon/Legends|Celanon]] or [[Ithor/Legends|Ithor]]. In [[17 ABY/Legends|17 ABY]], after a failed Imperial offensive, Pellaeon's forces were driven back to [[Bastion/Legends|Bastion]] and Agamar once more came under New Republic control.<ref name="EGTW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

===Yuuzhan Vong War===
{{Quote|I think your reading of these people, of their respect for tradition and family, is accurate. We know they contributed much to the effort against the Imperials, and they suffered for it. Keyan Farlander was but one of their sons and daughters that flew from here to wage war against the Empire.''"<br />"''But?''"<br />"''Some are capable of shouldering burdens for light-years, and others just kilometers.|[[Elegos A'Kla]] and Leia Organa Solo discuss Agamar|<ref name="DTI:O" />}}
Agamar remained part of the New Republic by the time of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]]. In [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], as the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] closed in on Republic space, a [[University of Agamar]] [[Xenoarchaeology/Legends|xenoarchaeological]] survey team, led by [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Anki Pace]], discovered the mummified remains of [[Mongei Shai]] on [[Bimmiel/Legends|Bimmiel]]. When the University administrators lost contact with the team, they asked the Jedi to investigate. [[Corran Horn/Legends|Corran Horn]] and [[Ganner Rhysode]] located the survey team, but were forced to evacuate them back to Agamar after the discovery of more Yuuzhan Vong on the planet.<ref name="DTI:O" />

[[File:AgamarNEC.png|thumb|right|250px|Agamar]]
Around the same time, former New Republic [[Chief of State (New Republic)/Legends|Chief of State]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]], having failed to make the Senate accept the threat posed by the Yuuzhan Vong, decided to warn Outer Rim worlds directly. Her first stop was Agamar where, together with New Republic scientist [[Danni Quee]], she stressed the imminent threat posed to all worlds in the Outer Rim and urged them to combine their forces. Organa Solo's impassioned plea was warmly received by the [[Agamarian Council]], but powerful individuals within Agamarian society sought to rebuild their world rather than risk their people in another war. Though the Council could not commit to military action, they did agree to her request to take in refugees from worlds already attacked by the Yuuzhan Vong. Not long after Organa Solo's visit, the Agamarians sent every available ship to assist in the [[Evacuation of Dubrillion|evacuation]] of [[Dubrillion/Legends|Dubrillion]]. Several were lost in a subsequent attack by the Yuuzhan Vong.<ref name="DTI:O" /> Agamar's large amounts of land made it a natural choice for the sudden increase in population, and it was soon serving as a clearing station for refugees from other worlds, including [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]].<ref name="NJOS" /> Nevertheless, the world quickly became overstretched with the influx of refugees<ref name="DTI:O" /> and the New Republic started organizing colonies to transport them further towards the Core Worlds.<ref name="DTII:R" /> As the extragalactic invaders continued to approach, the New Republic eventually began to evacuate the Agamarians themselves, transporting them to transit points including [[Gyndine/Legends|Gyndine]].<ref name="NJOS" /> The price of passage from Agamar quickly rose, and many independent captains took their ships there to make a profit from the mass evacuation.<ref name="DTII:R" />

Agamar's location on a hyperlane linking the Republic to its new allies in the Imperial Remnant made it an important world to hold and, while the refugee operation was ongoing, Admiral [[Traest Kre'fey]] utilized it as a staging area for New Republic forces. However, Agamar lay directly in the Yuuzhan Vong's path, and as the Republic realized that it couldn't hold both Agamar and Ithor, Chief of State [[Borsk Fey'lya]] made the decision to all but abandon Agamar, instructing Kre'fey to focus on defending Ithor.<ref name="NJOS" /> [[Deign Lian]], serving under [[Shedao Shai]], was given the task of planning a major [[Battle of Ithor|assault]] on Ithor, after first leading a feint at Agamar. They would then return to complete the invasion of Agamar.<ref name="DTII:R" />

Significant numbers of Agamarians had been evacuated by the time the world fell to the Yuuzhan Vong. Even so, Agamarians were among the groups hit hardest by the invaders. The abandonment of Agamar, along with other worlds in the Outer Rim, caused some unrest within the New Republic. Though it was justified as necessary to protect more strategically important worlds, there were many who suggested that it was the worlds that lacked strong representation in the Senate that were left to fall.<ref name="NJOS" />

===Later history===
[[File:Sith_forces_over_Agamar.jpg|thumb|left|270px|The ''War Hammer'' deploys starfighters over Agamar.]]
At some point between the end of the Yuuzhan Vong War in [[29 ABY/Legends|29 ABY]] and the start of the [[Second Galactic Civil War]] in [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], Agamar once more came under Imperial control. By [[130 ABY]], the [[Fel Empire|Empire]] had [[Sith–Imperial War|taken control]] of much of the galaxy from the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]]. After [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Darth Krayt]] attempted to depose Emperor [[Roan Fel]], the Empire split into two, with Agamar becoming part of Fel's [[Empire-in-exile]].<ref name="TEA" />

In [[137 ABY]], Fel's Empire formed an alliance with the surviving forces of the Galactic Alliance to oppose the Sith. With rumors of Krayt's death, the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] felt the time had come for them too to join the fight and Agamar was chosen for a meeting between the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] and Fel. News of the rendezvous soon reached the Imperial [[Regent/Legends|regent]], [[Morlish Veed]], who ordered [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Rulf Yage]] to lead an [[Operation: Thunderstroke|assault]] on the meeting.<ref name="Legacy43">[[Legacy (2006) 43|''Legacy'' (2006) 43]]</ref> The Fel loyalist Moff [[Morrigan Corde|Nyna Calixte]] traveled to Agamar to warn the allies, landing her starfighter at a distant farm so as not to alarm either party. Paying a [[Unidentified Agamarian farmer|native farmer]] to hide her vessel, Calixte proceeded to the meeting aboard a borrowed Agamarian beast, disguised in the farmer's cloak and hat. The Imperial arrived at the meeting site shortly after Fel reached an agreement with [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[K'Kruhk]] to coordinate future attacks against the Sith. However, the [[First Sith Imperial Strikeforce]], led by Yage's [[Pellaeon-class Star Destroyer|''Pellaeon''-class Star Destroyer]], the ''[[War Hammer]]'', had already emerged from hyperspace in orbit of Agamar and engaged Fel's own [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]], the [[Dauntless (Pellaeon-class)|''Dauntless'']].<ref name="Legacy45" />

While the battle continued in orbit, the Jedi and Fel's [[Imperial Knight]]s were soon confronted by a Sith strike team. Working together, the two groups were able to see Fel safely back to his [[Defender One|shuttle]], though Fel's daughter, [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Marasiah Fel]], was captured by the Sith during the evacuation. Despite taking heavy damage, the ''Dauntless'' held off the attacking Sith-Imperial force long enough for Fel's shuttle to clear the planet, but was destroyed soon after.<ref name="Legacy46">[[Legacy (2006) 46|''Legacy'' (2006) 46]]</ref>

==Inhabitants==
{{Quote|Dod Nobrin of Agamar.''"<br />"''I'm Dod, this is my brother Fod. Also from Agamar. This is my brother Lod.''"<br />"''Also from Agamar.''"<br />"''Oyah. That's right. You're pretty sharp for a city man.|An Imperial officer and Garik Loran, as Loran, Wedge Antilles, and Myn Donos sneak into Storinal as Agamarians|<ref name="XW:WS" />}}
The Agamarian settlers were mostly Human,<ref name="EGPM" /> though at least some other [[Species/Legends|species]] were present on the planet, including Rodians,<ref name="RC:TC" /> and [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]] was the planet's primary language.<ref name="EGPM" /> Most inhabitants of the simple [[Agriworld/Legends|agriworld]] made a living as farmers, merchants and craftspeople,<ref name="XW:TOSG" /> and relied on each other's help to prosper.<ref name="DTI:O" /> Their rustic lifestyle necessitated a degree of stubbornness and durability, and as a result, Agamarians developed a reputation as unsophisticated rubes, famous for their apparent stupidity. This reputation developed during the days of the Old Republic and continued throughout the planet's time within the Galactic Empire, with them cast as stupid in many jokes told throughout the galaxy.<ref name="XW:WS" /> Agamar's ruling body was the Agamarian Council, whose delegates sat in Calna Muun and were led by a speaker.<ref name="DTI:O" /> During the time of the Old Republic, Agamar had a governor<ref name="ST" /> and was represented in the Senate by the senator for the Lahara sector.<ref name="HNN" /> During Agamar's time in the New Republic, it was represented directly in the Senate.<ref name="AOCI:HT">''[[The New Jedi Order: Agents of Chaos I: Hero's Trial]]''</ref>

[[File:Agamarians.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Keyan Farlander and a female Agamarian]]
Agamar's most famous resident was [[Keyan Farlander/Legends|Keyan Farlander]]. Farlander grew up on a mugruebe ranch in Tondatha<ref name="EGPM" /> during the early years of the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]]. Farlander was returning home from Calna Muun and saw the Imperial assault ship descending on his hometown. Arriving in Tondatha just as the Imperials opened fire, Farlander raced to his home, which was struck by enemy fire moments later. Though he survived with only minor injuries,<ref name="XW:TOSG" /> his [[Keyan Farlander's mother|mother]] and [[Keyan Farlander's father|father]]<ref name="EGPM" /> were killed and his sister [[Kitha Farlander|Kitha]] was badly burned. Following the massacre, Farlander moved to Calna Muun and eventually joined the Agamar Resistance. When he later attended Mon Mothma's rally, he was inspired to join the Alliance and began a new life training aboard the ''Independence'' as a starfighter pilot. A natural pilot with an [[Force-sensitive/Legends|affinity]] for [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], Farlander fought in many battles, including the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|assault]] on the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star]],<ref name="XW:TOSG" /> the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|evacuation]] of [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] on [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] and the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]. He later trained as a Jedi<ref name="WWNJO">{{InsiderCite|57|Who's Who in the New Jedi Order}}</ref> and served as a general during the Yuuzhan Vong War, playing a role in several battles including the [[Battle of Ebaq]]<ref name="DW">''[[The New Jedi Order: Destiny's Way]]''</ref> and the [[Battle of Yuuzhan'tar|Recapture of Coruscant]].<ref name="UF">''[[The New Jedi Order: The Unifying Force]]''</ref> News of Farlander's actions reached his homeworld and the people of Agamar were proud of their world's most famous son.<ref name="EGPM" />

Farlander was not the only Agamarian to join the Alliance as a starfighter pilot—[['Ndranth Poussan]], [[Sunnar Jan-lo]] and [[Breth Gart]] also joined the Rebellion after Mon Mothma's speech. Poussan had not yet completed training when a shortage of pilots led to him seeing action in the [[Battle of Brigia (Galactic Civil War)|Battle of Brigia]]. He was killed during the battle when his fighter collided with a [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN starfighter]]. Gart, who was only sixteen upon joining the Alliance, twice failed in his bid to become a pilot due to [[disorientation syndrome]], before finally succeeding on his third attempt. He was killed shortly after in a freak collision with the [[EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate/Legends|EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate]] [[Priam (starship)|''Priam'']] during a Rebel attack on [[Kalla VII]]. Jan-lo served as a pilot before being injured during an attack on the ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer [[Intrepid (Imperial I-class)|''Intrepid'']] and later began an extended assignment with [[Alliance Intelligence/Legends|Alliance Intelligence]]. All four had previously been involved in the Agamar Resistance, under the leadership of [[B'ante Hatcher]], who was a strong advocate of the Resistance's eventual membership in the Rebel Alliance.<ref name="XW:TOSG" />

Later, Choday Hrakness pursued a successful career with the New Republic, rising to the rank of captain. Rather than being embarrassed by the Agamarian stereotype, while in command of the ''Night Caller'', he helped Garik Loran to develop the stereotypical Agamarian character the latter would use to infiltrate Storinal. This stereotype cast members of Wraith Squadron as poor yokels, dressed in rough ponchos made from a heavy brown cloth, with shirts and pants made from the same material in a lighter weave, and completed by broad-rimmed hats. Beyond their appearance, the group played up to the reputation of foolish Agamarians through their pretense of searching for wives, explaining that the only half a dozen attractive Agamarian women were already married.<ref name="XW:WS" />

Similarly, Captain [[Rimsen]]'s commendable service record saw him rise to command of the New Republic [[Victory I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Victory I''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Corusca Fire]]'' by the start of the Yuuzhan Vong War. Rimsen noticed unusual orders that effectively ensured that New Republic forces did not patrol near Dubrillion and [[Belkadan/Legends|Belkadan]]. When he learned of Leia Organa Solo's warning about the Yuuzhan Vong during a conversation with family, he surmised that Agamar was in danger and [[New Republic High Command/Legends|New Republic High Command]] was prepared to sacrifice his homeworld to prevent mass panic. Defying the orders of Chief of State Borsk Fey'lya, Rimsen took the ''Corusca Fire'' to Agamar in time to assist Traest Kre'fey in the [[Battle of Dantooine (Yuuzhan Vong War)|Battle of Dantooine]].<ref name="NJOS" />

==Locations==
[[File:CalnaMuun.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Calna Muun]]
Agamar's [[Capital/Legends|capital]] was Calna Muun,<ref name="DTI:O" /> which was also the largest city on the planet<ref name="EGPM" /> and referred to as the "Big City" by the Agamarians.<ref name="XW:TOSG" /> Located on the coast, the city served as the planet's main starport<ref name="EGPM" /> and also had a harbor from which tourists could take rides along the floor of the Bil Da'Gari ocean in transparent [[Submarine/Legends|submersibles]].<ref name="RC:TC" /> The small town of Tondatha was not located far from Calna Muun, on the other side of one of the world's many binka forests. Despite its proximity to Calna Muun, Tondatha was considered a fairly backwater town by even the native Agamarians, including some of its own residents.<ref name="XW:TOSG" />

[[File:Tondatha.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Tondatha]]
The Agamarian Council was housed in the [[Council Center]] in Calna Muun. Due to the Center's close proximity to the sea, the ocean had a clear influence on the architecture. Office balconies offered a view of the ocean to the north of the city, while the council chamber itself had an oceanic motif. The wooden floors, wall panels and furnishing were examples of high quality Agamarian craftsmanship, with the desks for Council delegates rising out of the floor like waves, leaping fish attached to the floor by wooden streams of water, and wooden birds fixed to the walls and ceiling by the tips of their wings. Even the speaker's podium was designed to resemble a stone sticking out of the waves around the base. Elsewhere, the high-ceilinged hallways were open to help keep the Center cool in the warm climate. Where pillars and archways divided the corridor into segments, [[Hologram/Legends|holographic]] art depicted Agamarian history and culture.<ref name="DTI:O" />

Agamar was also home to the University of Agamar, which boasted one of the largest xenoarchaeology departments in both the Old and New Republics. The University was involved in most large excavations throughout the galaxy, including such important sites as the [[Great Jedi Library/Legends|Jedi ruins]] on [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]].<ref name="GORW">''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Agamar was created during the development of the [[1993]] [[LucasArts]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']] to serve as the homeworld of the game's player character, Keyan Farlander. The planet was not actually established in the game itself, but in [[Rusel DeMaria]]'s accompanying novella, ''[[The Farlander Papers]]'', which told Farlander's story.<ref name="FP" /> However, the original floppy disk version of the game used "Agamar" as one of the copy protection codes.<ref name="XW">[[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']]</ref> Farlander's story continued in ''[[X-Wing: The Official Strategy Guide]]'', also by DeMaria, which contained more information about Agamar.<ref name="XW:TOSG" />

Much of Agamar's history was established in later sources. The planet has been referenced in several guidebooks, including entries in ''[[The Essential Guide to Planets and Moons]]'', the ''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' and ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''.<ref name="EGPM" /><ref name="SWE">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref><ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|I|14|Agamar}}</ref> Agamar has also featured in narrative works, including [[The New Jedi Order: Dark Tide I: Onslaught|''Dark Tide I: Onslaught'']] and [[The New Jedi Order: Dark Tide II: Ruin|''Dark Tide II: Ruin'']], part of [[Star Wars: The New Jedi Order|''The New Jedi Order'']] series of novels,<ref name="DTI:O" /><ref name="DTII:R" /> and the [[Star Wars: Legacy: Monster|''Monster'']] arc of the ''[[Star Wars: Legacy]]'' [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] series.<ref name="Legacy45" />

The [[Star Wars Insider 23|''Star Wars Insider'' 23]] article "[[LucasArts Update]]: The Creation Story" by [[Sue Seserman]], released in fall [[1994]], included some early plot details about the LucasArts video game ''[[Star Wars: Dark Forces]]'', which was due to be released [[1995|the following year]]. The article mentions a Rebel base on Agamar as one of the newly created locations which would be visited by the player character, [[Kyle Katarn]].<ref name="Insider23">{{InsiderCite|23|LucasArts Update}}</ref> Agamar did not appear in the final game, however, and the only [[Tak Base|Rebel base]] visited by Katarn is instead on the planet [[Talay/Legends|Talay]].<ref name="DF">''[[Star Wars: Dark Forces]]''</ref>
